terms.meaning: Shivaji's council of eight ministers. The Peshwa was the most important.
The Prime Minister of the Maratha king, who later ran the government.
The Coromandel coast (coastal Tamil Nadu and Andhra) and its hinterland, a Mughal province with Arcot as capital.

items.name: Why the Mughals declined
items.formula: Weak kings after Aurangzeb (1707), and the raids of Nadir Shah and Ahmed Shah Abdali.
items.example: Nadir Shah (1739) took the Peacock throne and the Kohinoor.

items.name: Peshwa rule
items.formula: Seven Peshwas ruled for about 100 years, 1713-1818.

items.name: Balaji Vishwanath (1713-20)
items.formula: Signed the treaty of Delhi with the Mughal Emperor.
items.example: He won the right to collect taxes from six Deccan subhas.

items.name: Baji Rao I (1720-40)
items.formula: Came to power at 20; took Hyderabad, Malwa, Gujarat and Bundelkhand, and attacked Delhi.

items.name: Balaji Baji Rao (1740-61)
items.formula: Spread Maratha power to Punjab, Orissa and parts of Tamil Nadu.
items.example: His rule ended with the defeat at Panipat.

items.name: Third Battle of Panipat
items.formula: 14 January 1761: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas.
items.example: Weaker Marathas gave the British their chance.

items.name: Cause of the Carnatic wars
items.formula: After the Nawab of Arcot died, Chand Saheb (backed by the French) and Mohammad Ali (backed by the British) fought for the throne.
items.example: Clive led the British; Dupleix led the French.

items.name: Results of the three Carnatic wars
items.formula: First: French won (Treaty of Aix-la-chapelle). Second: British kept Arcot, French Hyderabad. Third: British won.
items.example: After the third, the French were sidelined.

items.name: Why the French lost
items.formula: They neglected trade for politics, had a weaker navy and quarrelling officials.
items.example: The French company was under the government; the British one was private.

items.name: Why Siraj-ud-Daula clashed with the British
items.formula: They fortified Fort William in Calcutta without his permission and abused tax concessions.

items.name: Battle of Plassey (1757)
items.formula: Clive won because the Nawab's general Mir Jafar betrayed Siraj for the promise of becoming Nawab.
items.example: Mir Jafar was to pay 17 crores 70 lakh rupees; Aminchand arranged the deal.

items.name: Results of Plassey
items.formula: Mir Jafar became a puppet Nawab; the Company got the Twenty four paraganas.
items.example: It laid the foundation of British rule in India and led to Buxar.

mistakes.text: Plassey (1757) was British against Siraj; the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was Abdali against the Marathas.
"Shivaji II" was Peshwa Baji Rao I, not Shivaji's son.
The French won the first Carnatic war; the British won only in the end.
